WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY As a Program Manager, you will use your knowledge and experience to optimize business results and customer experience by: Managing and supporting real property projects to include supporting RPMS budgeting, auding, reporting business line and general RPMS administrative tasks.

Achieving organizational objectives by contributing information and recommendations to strategic plans and reviews; preparing and completing action plans; implementing project plans, assessing quality and customer-service standards.

Collaborating with other RPMS Branch Chiefs, ASA components, PSC and RLO to assist the RPMS Director in the accomplishment of multiple administrative and financial tasks associated with externally driven assignments and deadlines.

Enhancing RPMS and organization reputation by accepting ownership for accomplishing new and different requests; exploring opportunities to add value to job accomplishments, improve customer service and grow the business line.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Minimum Qualifications: You must have one year of specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Providing leadership, management and direction to a staff who support personnel involved in real property, facilities management; Initiating, managing, planning, scheduling, and implementing construction projects of varying complexity; Coordinating and integrating activities with senior management and program managers in providing effective solutions; Providing advice to senior level management involving the adoption of new procedures and programs to improve efficiency of operations.

Documenting experience: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE. Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience.

In addition to describing duties performed, applicants must provide the exact dates of each period of employment (from MM/YY to MM/YY) and the number of hours worked per week if part time.

As qualification determinations cannot be made when resumes do not include the required information, failure to provide this information may result in disqualification. Applicants are encouraged to use the USAJOBS Resume Builder to develop their federal resume.

Do not copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational application questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record.

In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to gain employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

If such experience is on a part-time basis, you must provide the average number of hours worked per week as well as the beginning and ending dates of the experience so it can be fully credited. OPM Qualification General Policies Website

IDAGIO is the leading streaming service for classical music, based in Berlin and part of IDAGIO Group. The Group spans streaming, recordings, and live music partnerships, globally. Our director initiates projects across all of it: recording partnerships with orchestras, licensing talks with international labels, concert-hall collaborations in Taiwan and Japan, and new ventures.
These initiatives move fast and span many time zones. We are looking for the person at the director's side who keeps them all on track.
Tasks
You are the assistant to the sole director of IDAGIO Group and work with him daily. He travels extensively and meets industry leaders, orchestras, and institutions across Asia, Europe and the US. Every trip produces introductions, ideas, and commitments. Your job is to make sure none of them get lost. You track every thread, follow up with every party, and hold everyone to agreed deadlines, including the director.
Beyond that, you coordinate selected projects across the Group's Berlin companies, working with their Managing Directors. Decisions sit with the director and the Managing Directors. Keeping things moving sits with you.
Assistant and project support to the director
Track and follow up on the projects and partnerships the director runs across the Group. You keep an up-to-date overview of status, owners, and next steps at all times.
Maintain deadlines and flag slipping dates early. You chase open items without being asked.
Prepare agendas, briefings, and follow-ups for meetings. Maintain trackers and status summaries.
Coordinate scheduling, information flow, and documentation across internal and external stakeholders, from orchestra managements to distribution partners.
Project coordination for Moto Lab
Moto Lab Partners is the Group's newest venture: it supports classical artists and institutions in building their international presence and careers, from recordings and concert videos to release strategy and promotion.
Coordinate Moto Lab's projects from start to finish, whatever their shape: a release, a concert video production, a marketing campaign, or a partner engagement.
Act as the central point of contact between everyone involved: artists and their management, orchestras, production crews, distributors, agencies, and internal teams.
Track each project's timeline from planning through delivery, follow up on deliverables, and support project and budget administration until everything is complete and approved.

Several years of professional experience, typically 2 to 5, in an assistant, coordination, project management, or artist management role. This should not be your first job. You have managed deadlines across multiple stakeholders and worked alongside a demanding senior principal before.
A firm understanding of classical music and the industry around it: repertoire, orchestras, how recordings and releases work. A background in classical music (studies, an orchestra, a label, an agency, a concert hall) is a strong plus.
Proactive and organized by temperament. You take ownership, chase without being prompted, and flag problems early.
Comfortable running several projects in parallel and prioritizing against deadlines.
Clear, structured communication and documentation. Status is transparent to everyone at any time.
Fluent German and English (C1 or better, spoken and written). Japanese or Mandarin is a real plus given our partners in Japan and Taiwan.
Based in Berlin or willing to relocate. Occasional flexibility for calls with Asia or the US and for concert or recording dates in the evening.

A rare vantage point: you work directly with the director of a music group active between Europe and Asia, and you see every initiative across it.
Real responsibility from day one. The role exists because these projects matter and need an owner.
A small, senior, international team in Berlin with short decision paths.
Salary range: €42,000–50,000 gross/year, depending on experience.
Send a short cover note, your CV, and your earliest possible start date to apply. Tell us about one person or project you supported where your follow-through made the difference.
IDAGIO and the IDAGIO Group value diversity. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements.

You will serve as an Environmental expert and will be responsible for leading and managing many aspects of the BRAC Environmental Program.
You will lead and manage the annual gathering of environmental requirements and supporting cost estimates in the NORM (the Normalization of Data) database.
You will provide oversight for the maintenance and operations to the NORM database hosted by NAVFAC's Information Technology Center.
You will provide management oversight for the numerous Knowledge-Based Corporate Reporting System (KBCRS) reports throughout the year to DoD that reflect program costs and milestones.
You will lead environmental programmatic initiatives, tiger teams and technical efforts across the PMO.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector performing duties such as: 1) leading coordination and negotiations with federal and state regulatory agencies (e.g., EPA, state environmental departments) on complex programmatic or funding issues; and preparing written products-including briefs, point papers, reports, and correspondence-to present and defend program decisions to senior DoD, DON, or Congressional stakeholders.2) Experience leading environmental program management for a complex federal environmental restoration or compliance program, including developing and validating cost estimates, tracking milestones (such as RIP and RC), and preparing programmatic reporting for senior leadership and Congress 3)Experience analyzing and resolving complex program-level challenges, including reconciling system-to-system financial execution data, addressing budget shortfalls, and developing strategic workarounds to ensure environmental cleanup milestones remain on schedule.4)Experience directing federal environmental financial reporting processes, including POM budget formulation, Environmental Liabilities (EL) reporting, and ensuring data integrity across national-level tracking systems (such as NORM and KBCRS) to meet federal audit-readiness standards.5)Experience interpreting and applying federal environmental laws, regulations, and policies (e.g., CERCLA, RCRA, NEPA, SARA) to guide, evaluate, and report on environmental restoration, compliance, or real property disposal programs at an enterprise level.

Buscamos un/a Jefe de Proyectossemi-senior para liderar proyectos mensuales y continuos en Lisit. En este rol nos enfocamos en asegurar una ejecución ordenada, medible y alineada a los objetivos, con gobernanza, control y comunicación efectiva con todas las partes involucradas.

s.h: Responsabilidades clave (sobre el día a día)
s.t:
Planificar y ordenar el trabajo del proyecto: objetivos, alcance, cronograma, recursos, presupuesto, hitos y entregables.
Coordinar equipos internos, externos y proveedores, asignando tareas, seguimiento del desempeño y resolución de conflictos entre áreas.
Conducir el control de avance, alcance y calidad, gestionando cambios y reportando el estado del proyecto a la gerencia.
Gestionar presupuesto y riesgos (tecnológicos y operacionales), con planes de mitigación y escalamiento cuando corresponda.
Ejercer gobierno y documentación: actas/minutas, actualización documental y gestión de lecciones aprendidas, asegurando cumplimiento metodológico.
Gestionar stakeholders y expectativas del negocio, coordinando reuniones de seguimiento y obteniendo aprobaciones formales.
Impulsar la gestión del cambio: capacitaciones, apoyo a la adopción de nuevas tecnologías, gestión de resistencia y acompañamiento de la transición a operación.

s.h: Lo que valoramos para que la persona se desempeñe con éxito
s.t:
Experiencia en coordinación y liderazgo de proyectos con múltiples actores (internos/externos/proveedores) y seguimiento de entregables.
Enfoque en resultados : criterio para definir éxito, medir progreso y actuar ante desvíos de tiempo, alcance, costos y calidad.
Comunicación clara y oportuna con usuarios clave, gerencia y equipos de trabajo.
Organización y documentación : orden en actas, minutas, trazabilidad y lecciones aprendidas.
Gestión de conflicto y facilitación: capacidad de destrabar entre áreas y sostener una comunicación fluida.
Gestión del riesgo : anticipación, monitoreo y escalamiento con criterio.
Actitud colaborativa y orientada al cliente: coherencia entre objetivos, necesidades del negocio y ejecución técnica/operacional.

Elaborar actas y minutas. Mantener documentación actualizada. Gestionar lecciones aprendidas. Asegurar cumplimiento metodológico.
Experiencia coordinando consultoras y proveedores, con validación de entregables y seguimiento de SLA y compromisos.
Conocimiento práctico de gestión de cambios (capacitaciones y adopción de tecnologías) y manejo de resistencia.

Basic Requirements Degree: behavioral or social science; or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR Combination of education and experience that provided the applicant with knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

OR Four years of appropriate experience that demonstrated that the applicant has acquired knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field. Die impulsarbeit gmbh entwickelt in Winterthur ein neues Förderprogramm für junge Frauen mit Fluchthintergrund.
Ziel ist die persönliche, gesellschaftliche und wirtschaftliche Emanzipation der Teilnehmerinnen. Die Frauen sollen ihre Ressourcen und Handlungsmöglichkeiten erweitern und schrittweise die Voraussetzungen schaffen, ihr Leben selbstbestimmt und möglichst unabhängig von staatlicher Unterstützung gestalten zu können.
Für den Aufbau und die fachliche Entwicklung des Programms suchen wir per 1. Oktober 2026 eine Projektleiterin (40 %). Die Stelle ist zunächst auf ein Jahr befristet.
Ein Programm mit Zeit für Entwicklung
Für die Aufbau- und Entwicklungsphase stehen substanzielle private Mittel zur Verfügung. Dadurch kann das Programm ohne kurzfristigen Finanzierungs-, Vermittlungs- oder Mengendruck entwickelt werden.
Unterschiedliche Ansätze können sorgfältig erprobt, ausgewertet und weiterentwickelt werden. Eine externe Wirkungsmessung begleitet das Programm und stellt sicher, dass Erkenntnisse systematisch in die kontinuierliche Qualitätsentwicklung einfliessen.
Ziel ist ein fachlich fundiertes, lernendes und langfristig anschlussfähiges Fördermodell. Die Zusammenarbeit mit Gemeinden, Kanton, Fachstellen und bestehenden Integrationsstrukturen ist ausdrücklich erwünscht.
Zwei Arbeitstage – zwei unterschiedliche Erfahrungsräume
Die 40%-Stelle verteilt sich grundsätzlich auf zwei Arbeitstage pro Woche.
1. Tag: Förderung, Arbeitsintegration und Fallarbeit
Die Teilnehmerinnen arbeiten in einem realen betrieblichen Umfeld und sammeln konkrete Arbeitserfahrungen. Die Projektleiterin begleitet diesen Prozess fachlich und individuell.

· arbeitsintegrative Begleitung

· individuelle Förderplanung

· Fallarbeit

· Erkennen und Aktivieren vorhandener Ressourcen

· Reflexion der Erfahrungen im Betrieb

· Entwicklung beruflicher und persönlicher Perspektiven

· Zusammenarbeit mit Betrieben, Fachstellen und weiteren Beteiligten

· Planung geeigneter nächster Entwicklungsschritte
2. Tag: Waldtag und individuelles Coaching
Der zweite Tag schafft bewusst einen anderen Rahmen. Ein Teil des Tages findet gemeinsam im Wald statt. Natur, Bewegung, gemeinsames Tun und Gespräche eröffnen andere Zugänge zu Ressourcen, Beziehungen und persönlichen Themen.
Ergänzend finden individuelle Coachings statt. Hier können persönliche Ziele, aktuelle Herausforderungen, Ressourcen und nächste Schritte vertieft bearbeitet werden.
Beide Tage gehören zusammen: konkrete Erfahrung und Arbeitsintegration auf der einen Seite, Reflexion, individuelle Entwicklung und Stabilisierung auf der anderen.

Wir suchen eine Frau mit einem Abschluss in Sozialer Arbeit FH oder einem fundierten fachlichen Hintergrund in kunstbasierten, kunstpädagogischen oder kunsttherapeutischen Methoden.

s.h: Von Vorteil sind Kenntnisse und praktische Erfahrungen mit
s.t:

workspace using the Large Language Models (LLMs).

operation team, with a focus on selecting and experimenting the best LLM model for
integrating into production workflows. You will evaluate, select, and operationalize LLM
solutions (including hybrid approaches) across high-resource languages (HRLs), low-resource
languages (LRLs), and low resources content types, leveraging Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
services (e.g., Vertex AI, AutoML Translation, BigQuery) or any cloud providers to balance
quality, scalability, latency, and cost.

translate experimental capabilities into production-grade systems, while ensuring
measurable impact on translation quality, turnaround time, and cost efficiency

Evaluate and benchmark GCP-native models and services alongside external
vendors, making recommendations based on quality, latency, and cost

Drive automation (scripting, APIs, orchestration) to reduce manual effort and operational
overhead.
Productionization & Cross-functional Execution
Define requirements and partner with Engineering to productionize LLM solutions.
Partner with Engineering and MLOps to deploy and monitor models on GCP infrastructure, ensuring reliability, observability, and cost control.
Write clear PRDs and operational specs covering data flow, model behavior, evaluation, and guardrails.
Work with MLOps/LLMOps to ensure monitoring, versioning, and lifecycle management of models.
Quality & Performance Management
Establish quality frameworks combining automated metrics and human evaluation.
Monitor model performance in production and drive continuous improvement loops.
Own trade-off decisions across quality, cost, and speed, with clear reporting to stakeholders.
Stakeholder & Program Leadership
Act as the primary point of contact for ML-driven solutions across internal teams and vendors.
Align stakeholders on roadmap, priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Lead cross-functional initiatives across time zones.
Data & Insights
Partner with Data/Engineering to build dashboards tracking: Model performance (quality metrics)
Cost per word/request
Throughput and latency
Enable data-driven decision-making for both technical and business stakeholders.

3+ years working with MT, LLM, or ML-driven language systems in production including deployment.
1+ years in localization operations (CMS/TMS) in a tech or platform environment.
Proven experience driving end-to-end programs, not just execution within a single function.

Hands-on experience fine-tuning LLMs for multilingual use cases or implementing RAG pipelines for grounded translation.

Narvar is growing! We are hiring a Technical Project Manager to drive our most complex, multi-team engineering initiatives — the ones with no single owning team, where progress depends on getting the sequencing right across groups that don't naturally coordinate with each other.
This is not a status-reporting role. You won't be writing production code, but you will build and maintain the real dependency graph behind a project: which team's output blocks which other team's start, where the critical path actually runs, and what has to happen in what order for the whole thing to land.

You'll follow technical discussions closely enough to spot those dependencies before they become blockers, and you'll proactively pull in the right people — across engineering, product, design, data, or leadership — before gaps turn into delays.

Dependency mapping and critical path management
Map cross-team dependencies for projects that span multiple engineering teams with no single owning team — identify what blocks what, and in what order work needs to happen
Maintain a live view of the critical path, not just individual teams' task lists, and flag when a slip in one team changes the achievable timeline for others
Surface hidden or emerging dependencies before they become blockers, particularly ones that no single team has visibility into because they sit at the seams between teams
Distill the graph into concise, honest updates for non-technical stakeholders and leadership — what's driving the timeline, what's at risk, and why
Cross-functional coordination
Identify when product management, design, data, legal, or other stakeholders need to be looped in — and act on it proactively, without waiting for engineers to flag it
Recognize when a dependency crosses team boundaries and make sure the teams on both sides of it are actually talking to each other, not just individually on track
Chase down answers, escalate when needed, and keep work moving forward
Serve as the connective tissue across engineering and adjacent functions throughout the delivery lifecycle — especially where no single team is positioned to see the whole picture
Technical context and decision support
Follow technical discussions closely enough to grasp the tradeoffs being made — architecture decisions, infrastructure choices, API design, build vs. buy — and understand how those choices ripple into other teams' work
Reason about sequencing implications of technical decisions: does this choice change what can be built in parallel versus what must be serial?
Surface implications of technical decisions for timeline, scope, or other teams
Know when a decision warrants broader input and facilitate getting it, without creating unnecessary process overhead
Documentation and operational hygiene
Keep the dependency graph, specs, decisions, and timelines documented and accessible
Ensure decisions made in Slack or ad-hoc meetings don't get lost, especially ones that affect teams beyond the room they were made in
Make it easy for anyone joining a project mid-stream to get up to speed quickly — including understanding why the sequencing is what it is

Systems and dependency thinking: You can look at multiple teams' plans and identify where they interlock — where a change in one ripples into another — even when no one team has full visibility into the whole
Technical fluency: You don't need to write code, but you need to follow engineering conversations comfortably — architecture diagrams, system tradeoffs, sprint planning — without hand-holding
Project management experience: 4+ years managing complex, multi-team software projects with several workstreams and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment — ideally including projects with no single owning team
Strong written communication: Able to distill a complex dependency picture into crisp, accurate updates for non-technical audiences
Proactive by default: You identify when to loop someone in without being asked, and you follow through without needing to be chased
Calm under ambiguity: Able to drive clarity and keep work moving without waiting for perfect information, a fully defined process, or a single team to own the outcome
Cross-functional credibility: Comfortable holding a room with engineers, product managers, designers, and executives — and earning trust from all of them

Prior experience as a software engineer, QA, or technical analyst
Familiarity with agile and scrum methodologies; experience with tools like Jira, Linear, or Shortcut, especially for modeling cross-team dependencies
Experience running programs (not just single-team projects) — i.e., initiatives coordinated across multiple teams toward a shared outcome
Experience working with distributed or remote engineering teams

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency: Psychologists must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section A, paragraph 3j.

Education: Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re-specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re-specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and The specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

NOTE: The applicant must provide an official transcript and/or certificate documenting the completion of the re-specialization program, which includes completion of an APA or CPA internship. OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

AND Internship: Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern.

OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement.

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

s.h: In 6 years of existence, we’ve managed to
s.t:

Why this role exists
Pennylane is one of Europe's fastest-growing fintechs, building the financial operating system for SMBs and their accountants. Growth at our pace creates a constant stream of high-stakes, cross-functional initiatives that don't sit neatly inside any one team such as entering new markets, redesigning pricing, launching e-invoicing ahead of regulation.
This role owns those initiatives. You'll work directly with the VP Strategic Initiatives (and, through him, the executive committee) to take our most important initiatives from a blank page to a shipped outcome. It's a rare seat: broad exposure to how a scale-up actually makes its biggest decisions, real ownership from day one, and the kind of scope that builds a strong foundation for an operating role over time.
What you'll own
You'll lead selected priority initiatives end-to-end. For each, that means:
Framing the problem. Turn an ambiguous executive ambition into a structured plan: the hypothesis, the analysis that tests it, the milestones, and the definition of success.
Driving the work. Coordinate the product, commercial, finance, and ops teams needed to deliver. You're the person who makes sure it actually ships, on time and to the bar.
Doing the analysis yourself. Build the models, pull the data, and pressure-test the numbers that decisions rest on. You won't delegate the thinking.
Keeping the ExCo close. Report progress, risks, and recommendations crisply and often. When something is off track, they hear it from you first, with a proposed path forward.
Some initiatives you'll run start to finish. On others you'll be the extra set of hands on whatever matters most that quarter. Both require someone who's comfortable being handed a hard, undefined problem and trusted to figure it out.

5–10 years in top-tier management consulting and/or a VC-backed scale-up, with a track record of owning complex projects to completion in a fast-moving environment.
Exceptional analytical capabilities — you're fluent with data and models, and you use them to sharpen decisions, not decorate them.
Structured thinker and clear communicator who can make a complex trade-off legible to an executive audience in a page or a slide.
Genuinely comfortable with ambiguity: strong judgment, a bias to action, and the maturity to prioritize hard.
Fluent in French and English.
This is a role for a strategic thinker who likes to get their hands dirty. If that's you, we'd love to talk.

## Your Purpose ##
The LNG Manager is responsible for inspecting the construction and outfitting of the related LNG equipment and that fitting is done according to international regulation, ship-s contract, technical specifications, and builder standards.

This role is controlling the quality of the materials used, the compliance with regulation and with IGF Code and highlighting any discrepancies within the approved project.

Potential adjustments when minor technical issues are identified by this role, during the construction phase, may be recorded and shared within the Site team and new building division as lesson learnt to be implemented on next projects.

* Ensures that areas under the described discipline are built within the set timescale and in line with the approved technical design, contractual requirements, and functional requisites.
* Follows the installation and outfitting of all LNG equipment and piping maintaining accurate and up to date records of all activities and inspections.
* Attends project meetings and prepares progress reports.
* Ensures that all commissioning activities are held in accordance with the scope and the specifications, are approved by class and relevant authorities such us Flag and USCG representatives.
* Suggests minor adjustments as may be found necessary on site and follows implementation and development of any architectural / technical design change.
* Highlights relevant aspects of the approved design that can be improved for future constructions.
* Involves the Technical Site Specialist(s) during the construction and commissioning phase to ensure that technical accessibility and functionality of equipment is duly verified.
* Highlights relevant aspects of the ship-s design and technical features that might jeopardise the functional requisites and must be improved for the current project or can be improved for future constructions with new building department approval.
* Assists with Plan Approval activities as required.
## Your Journey so far ##
* Fluency in English, knowledge of Italian or French is a plus.
* A Degree relevant to shipbuilding or equivalent qualification or significant relevant experience is required, however no degree but proven experience in operations is also considered as validation for application.
* Substantial experience with delivering inspections of technical areas on ship-s building and or refitting projects or onboard cruise vessels in operations.
* Good knowledge of IGF Code.
* Good knowledge of piping, electrical machinery inspection is a plus as she/he may be requested to cooperate with the technical teams for the daily inspections included within the ship-s construction.
* Experience in a leadership position on board LNG vessels or cruise ships with LNG duty might be beneficial.
* Proficiency with the use of Microsoft Office (including Excel, MS Word, MS Project or equivalent and PowerPoint);
* Familiarity with Marine Rules and International Standards and Regulations.
* Ability to review new building specifications and to read and understand a variety of engineering drawings.
* Ability to review RCA and technical reports to ensure lesson learnt and their application during construction.
